chapters.title: Conversation and plans
chapters.description: Turn the foundations into short, useful exchanges about people, time, and plans.

lessons.title: Conversation and plans
lessons.subtitle: 話してみよう
lessons.description: Use greetings, names, days, and invitations to make a simple plan with someone.

vocabulary.title: こんにちは

exampleSentences.japanese: こんにちは。私は学生です。

vocabulary.notes: こんにちは is a daytime greeting; use こんばんは in the evening.

vocabulary.title: ありがとう

exampleSentences.japanese: ありがとうございます。

collocations: ありがとうございます。
vocabulary.notes: ありがとうございます is the polite form used in the lesson examples.

vocabulary.title: すみません

exampleSentences.japanese: すみません。駅はどこですか。
exampleSentences.translation: Excuse me. Where is the station?

collocations: すみません、お願いします。
vocabulary.notes: It can get someone's attention, apologize, or soften a request.

vocabulary.title: お願いします
vocabulary.notes: お願いします is a polite request expression; ください follows a noun or verb て-form.

vocabulary.title: 名前
vocabulary.notes: お名前 is the polite version used when asking another person's name.

vocabulary.title: 国

exampleSentences.japanese: あなたの国はどこですか。

vocabulary.notes: The question can be understood as asking which country someone is from.

vocabulary.title: 日本
vocabulary.notes: 日本 is also commonly read にっぽん in some names and formal contexts; this course uses にほん.

vocabulary.title: 日本語
vocabulary.notes: 語 means language in compounds such as 日本語.

vocabulary.title: 何
vocabulary.notes: 何 is often pronounced なん before some counters and particles, but なに is a useful base reading.

vocabulary.title: 誰
vocabulary.notes: 誰 asks about a person; 何 asks about a thing or action.

vocabulary.title: いつ

exampleSentences.japanese: いつ日本へ行きますか。
exampleSentences.translation: When are you going to Japan?

vocabulary.notes: いつ asks for a time without requiring a particular time word in the answer.

vocabulary.title: 今
vocabulary.notes: 今 can set the time for an action: 今、勉強します.

vocabulary.title: 午前
vocabulary.notes: 午前 is used with clock times to specify before noon.

vocabulary.title: 午後

exampleSentences.japanese: 午後、図書館へ行きます。
exampleSentences.translation: I go to the library in the afternoon.

vocabulary.notes: 午後 can mean the afternoon generally or the p.m. part of a clock time.

vocabulary.title: 昼
vocabulary.notes: 昼ご飯 means lunch; ご飯 can refer to a meal as well as cooked rice.

vocabulary.title: 夜
vocabulary.notes: 夜 is a natural time setting for evening and nighttime routines.

vocabulary.title: 毎週

exampleSentences.japanese: 毎週、図書館へ行きます。
exampleSentences.translation: I go to the library every week.

vocabulary.notes: Recurring 毎- time words normally do not need に.

vocabulary.title: 日曜日

exampleSentences.japanese: 日曜日に友達と会います。
exampleSentences.translation: I meet a friend on Sunday.

vocabulary.notes: Days of the week can take に when marking the time of a specific action.

vocabulary.title: 休む
vocabulary.notes: 休む can mean resting or being absent from school/work.

vocabulary.title: 読む

exampleSentences.translation: I read a book every day.

vocabulary.notes: 読む changes to 読みます in polite non-past speech.

vocabulary.title: 書く
vocabulary.notes: 書く is a godan verb; its polite form is 書きます.

vocabulary.title: 聞く
vocabulary.notes: Context determines whether 聞く means listen or ask.

vocabulary.title: する
vocabulary.notes: する forms many compound verbs, such as 勉強する.

vocabulary.title: 遊ぶ

exampleSentences.japanese: 日曜日に友達と遊びます。
exampleSentences.translation: I spend time with a friend on Sunday.

vocabulary.notes: With friends, 遊ぶ often means hanging out rather than playing a specific game.

vocabulary.title: 会う

exampleSentences.japanese: 日曜日に友達と会います。
exampleSentences.translation: I meet a friend on Sunday.

vocabulary.notes: と marks the person you meet in the example.

vocabulary.title: 帰る
vocabulary.notes: 帰る is a movement verb and uses へ or に for the destination.

vocabulary.title: 暑い
vocabulary.notes: 暑い describes weather or the outside temperature; 熱い describes hot things to touch or taste.

vocabulary.title: 涼しい
vocabulary.notes: 涼しい describes pleasantly cool weather, not cold weather.

vocabulary.title: 小さい
vocabulary.notes: 小さい directly modifies a noun before です or a noun phrase.

vocabulary.title: 古い
vocabulary.notes: 古い describes objects, buildings, and things with age; it is not normally used for people.

vocabulary.title: 忙しい
vocabulary.notes: 忙しい can describe a person's schedule or a busy day.

vocabulary.title: 一緒
vocabulary.notes: 一緒に is the common form before an action: together with someone.

vocabulary.title: 時々
vocabulary.notes: 時々 usually comes before the action it modifies.

vocabulary.title: ゆっくり

exampleSentences.japanese: ゆっくり話してください。

vocabulary.notes: ゆっくり is useful when asking for a slower pace in conversation.

grammar.title: ましょう
grammar.meaning: let's do V; a polite suggestion
grammar.intuition: ましょう turns a plan into a suggestion for the speaker and listener together.
usageConditions: Use it when suggesting a shared action.
It is more direct than ませんか and often follows an agreed plan.

examples.japanese: 一緒に行きましょう。
examples.translation: Let's go together.

examples.japanese: 日曜日に会いましょう。
examples.translation: Let's meet on Sunday.

examples.japanese: 一緒に勉強しましょう。
examples.translation: Let's study together.

examples.japanese: 駅で会いましょう。
examples.translation: Let's meet at the station.

commonMistakes: Use the verb stem before ましょう: 行きましょう, not 行くましょう.
ましょう includes the suggestion; do not add です after it.

grammar.title: ませんか
grammar.meaning: would you like to V?; a soft invitation
grammar.intuition: The negative question makes an invitation gentle and leaves room for the other person's choice.
usageConditions: Use it to invite someone to do an action with you.
A positive response can use ましょう.

examples.japanese: 一緒に勉強しませんか。
examples.translation: Would you like to study together?

examples.japanese: お茶を飲みませんか。
examples.translation: Would you like to drink tea?

examples.japanese: 一緒に昼ご飯を食べませんか。
examples.translation: Would you like to eat lunch together?

examples.japanese: 週末、映画を見ませんか。
examples.translation: Would you like to watch a movie this weekend?

commonMistakes: Do not use the dictionary form before か in this pattern.
This is an invitation, not simply a question about a negative action.

grammar.title: から…まで
grammar.formation: Starting point + から + ending point + まで
grammar.intuition: から marks where a range begins and まで marks where it ends.
usageConditions: Use it for time ranges, places, and other clear endpoints.
Either endpoint can be omitted when the context is obvious.

examples.japanese: 九時から五時まで勉強します。
examples.translation: I study from nine to five.

examples.japanese: 駅から大学まで電車で行きます。
examples.translation: I go by train from the station to the university.

examples.japanese: 駅から学校まで歩きます。
examples.translation: I walk from the station to school.

examples.japanese: 九時から五時まで働きます。
examples.translation: I work from nine to five.

commonMistakes: Keep the order start から end まで.
まで marks the endpoint, not the means of transport.

grammar.title: や
grammar.formation: Noun + や + noun; often followed by など when the list is explicitly incomplete
grammar.intuition: や gives examples from a larger group instead of presenting a complete list.
usageConditions: Use it when naming representative items.
Use と for a complete list of the items you mean.

examples.japanese: 机の上に本やノートがあります。
examples.translation: There are books, notebooks, and things like that on the desk.

examples.japanese: 日曜日は本や音楽を楽しみます。
examples.translation: On Sundays I enjoy books, music, and things like that.

examples.japanese: 店でりんごやバナナを買いました。
examples.translation: I bought things like apples and bananas at the shop.

examples.japanese: 机の上に本やノートがあります。
examples.translation: There are books, notebooks, and the like on the desk.

commonMistakes: や is not the usual particle for people you do something with.
The list with や is understood as incomplete.

grammar.title: てください
grammar.intuition: ください makes a request for an action polite and clear.
usageConditions: Use it for a direct but polite request.
The verb before ください must be in て-form.

examples.japanese: 名前を書いてください。
examples.translation: Please write your name.

examples.japanese: ゆっくり話してください。
examples.translation: Please speak slowly.

examples.japanese: ここに名前を書いてください。
examples.translation: Please write your name here.

examples.japanese: ドアを開けてください。
examples.translation: Please open the door.

commonMistakes: Use て-form, not ます-form: 書いてください, not 書きますください.
ください is part of the request pattern, not a standalone verb ending here.

grammar.title: とても
grammar.formation: Place とても before the adjective or adverb it strengthens.
grammar.intuition: とても increases the intensity of a description without changing its grammar.
usageConditions: Use it before an adjective or adverb.
It can describe a strong positive or negative degree.

examples.japanese: この本はとても面白いです。
examples.translation: This book is very interesting.

examples.japanese: 今日はとても暑いです。
examples.translation: It is very hot today.

examples.japanese: この町はとても静かです。
examples.translation: This town is very quiet.

examples.japanese: 今日はとても暑いです。
examples.translation: Today is very hot.

commonMistakes: Put とても before the description, not after です.
Do not confuse とても with ときどき, which describes frequency.

grammarContrasts.title: ませんか and ましょう
grammarContrasts.explanation: ませんか offers a gentle invitation and leaves the response open. ましょう presents a shared suggestion, often after both people are ready to agree.

examples.japanese: 一緒に勉強しませんか。
examples.translation: Would you like to study together?

examples.japanese: はい、勉強しましょう。
examples.translation: Yes, let's study.

exercises: Invite someone softly with ませんか.
Turn an accepted plan into a shared suggestion with ましょう.

grammarContrasts.title: から and まで
grammarContrasts.explanation: から marks the starting point of a range, while まで marks the endpoint. They commonly work as a pair for time and distance.

examples.japanese: 九時から勉強します。
examples.translation: I study from nine.

examples.japanese: 九時から五時まで勉強します。
examples.translation: I study from nine to five.

exercises: Mark the start of a schedule with から.
Add the end of the schedule with まで.

grammarContrasts.title: や and と
grammarContrasts.explanation: と presents a complete list or the person you act with. や gives representative examples from a larger, unfinished list.

examples.japanese: 本とノートがあります。
examples.translation: There are a book and a notebook.

examples.japanese: 本やノートがあります。
examples.translation: There are books, notebooks, and things like that.

exercises: Use と when the list is complete.
Use や when the list gives examples.

grammarContrasts.title: て-form and てください
grammarContrasts.explanation: The て-form connects actions or participates in other patterns. Adding ください turns it into a polite request.

examples.japanese: 本を読んで、勉強します。
examples.translation: I read a book and then study.

examples.japanese: 本を読んでください。
examples.translation: Please read the book.

exercises: Use て-form to connect two actions.
Add ください when asking someone to do the action.

grammarContrasts.title: 午前 and 午後
grammarContrasts.explanation: 午前 places a clock time before noon, while 午後 places it after noon. Both can set the time for a routine.

examples.japanese: 午前七時に起きます。
examples.translation: I get up at seven in the morning.

examples.japanese: 午後三時に会います。
examples.translation: I meet someone at three in the afternoon.

exercises: Use 午前 for a morning clock time.
Use 午後 for an afternoon clock time.

readings.title: 短い自己紹介
readings.passage: こんにちは。私は学生です。毎日、日本語を勉強します。日曜日は友達と会います。
readings.translation: Hello. I am a student. I study Japanese every day. On Sundays, I meet a friend.

questions.prompt: 毎日、何を勉強しますか。
questions.explanation: 毎日、日本語を勉強します。

questions.prompt: 日曜日にだれと会いますか。
questions.explanation: 日曜日は友達と会います。

readings.title: 一日の予定
readings.passage: 午前は大学へ行きます。午後は図書館で本を読みます。夜は家へ帰ります。日曜日は休みます。
readings.translation: In the morning I go to university. In the afternoon I read a book at the library. At night I return home. On Sunday I rest.

questions.prompt: 午後、どこで本を読みますか。
questions.explanation: 午後は図書館で本を読みます。

questions.prompt: 日曜日は何をしますか。

listening.title: 家族の紹介
listening.situation: A learner introduces a family member to a friend.
listening.transcript:
A：こちらは母です。
B：こんにちは。お名前は何ですか。
C：恵です。よろしくお願いします。

questions.prompt: Aさんはだれを紹介しますか。

listening.title: 一緒に行きませんか
listening.situation: Two friends make a Sunday plan.
listening.transcript:
A: 日曜日、一緒に図書館へ行きませんか。
B: はい、行きましょう。
A: 何時に会いますか。
B: 午後二時に会いましょう。

questions.prompt: 二人はいつ図書館へ行きますか。
questions.explanation: 日曜日、一緒に図書館へ行きませんか。
午後二時に会いましょう。

listening.title: 午前と午後
listening.situation: A learner explains a simple day's schedule.
listening.transcript:
A: 明日、何をしますか。
B: 午前は大学へ行きます。午後は図書館で勉強します。
A: 夜は？
B: 家へ帰ります。

questions.prompt: 午前、どこへ行きますか。
questions.explanation: 午前は大学へ行きます。
午後は図書館で勉強します。
